create.name: Nagarjuna Madrid
create.bio:
Nagarjuna Madrid is a Tibetan Buddhist meditation and study centre in the Spanish capital, belonging to the Gelug school of Lama Tsong Khapa, the lineage of the Dalai Lama, whom it names as its inspiration. Lama Thubten Yeshe established it in 1983, and it remains affiliated to the Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition (FPMT), the international network he set up with Lama Zopa Rinpoche in 1975. Its resident teacher is Geshe Jamphel Gyaltsen, born in Kham in 1967, who fled to India in 1989 and spent over two decades at Sera Je Monastery before gaining the Geshe Lharampa degree in 2008. The centre is run by Fernando Fernández, who has guided its meditation courses for more than ten years.

Its programme mixes structured Buddhist study with practice: weekend courses, often attended in person or online, weekly classes on mind training, Sunday morning intensives in calm-abiding meditation on the breath, retreats and a Wednesday evening cycle of sutra readings. Visiting lamas teach there regularly. The Spanish-language YouTube channel, running since 2011, keeps recordings of full teachings, including a multi-part commentary on the Diamond Sutra, a long Lam Rim retreat series, Mahamudra sessions and question-and-answer evenings with Geshe Gyaltsen.

courses.title: Sutra del Corazón con S.E. Serkong Tsenshap Rimpoché
courses.description: A weekend of teachings from Serkong Tsenshap Rinpoche on the Heart Sutra, the condensed Prajnaparamita text on emptiness, attended in person in Madrid or online. Online attendance is 30€; members pay 30€ in person or 15€ online; ordained Sangha attend free.

courses.title: Intensivo de meditación de Sámatha
courses.description: A Sunday morning of calm-abiding meditation on the breath, alternating sitting and walking sessions, led by the centre's director Fernando Fernández, with time for questions at the end. Free for members.

free_resources.title: Recitación de Sutras
free_resources.description: A weekly Wednesday evening session reading short sutras from the Pali canon together, with an online entry link on the page.
